ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, AC is the diagonal of square ABCD, E is a point on BC, with $BE=1$. By folding $\triangle ABE$ along AE so that point B falls on point F on AC, what is the length of AB?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since quadrilateral ABCD is a square, \\
$\therefore$ AB = BC, $\angle$BCD = $\angle$B = $90^\circ$, $\angle$ECF = $\frac{1}{2}$ $\angle$BCD = $45^\circ$,\\
By the property of folding: $\angle$AFE = $\angle$B = $90^\circ$, FE = BE = 1,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle$CFE = $90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\triangle$ CEF is an isosceles right-angled triangle,\\
$\therefore$ CE = $\sqrt{2}$ FE = $\sqrt{2}$,\\
$\therefore$ BC = BE + CE = 1 + $\sqrt{2}$,\\
$\therefore$ AB = BC = \boxed{1 + \sqrt{2}};

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, AC is the diagonal of square ABCD, E is a point on BC, with $BE=1$. By folding $\triangle ABE$ along AE so that point B falls on point F on AC, what is the length of AB?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is a square ABCD, with A at the upper left, B at the lower left, C at the lower right, and D at the upper right; AC is the diagonal from A to C. Point E is located on the bottom side BC, and AE is also drawn in the figure. After folding, point B falls onto point F on diagonal AC; in the figure F is located inside AC, and EF is connected. Reasoning: Let the side length AB of the square be x. Since E is on BC, AB and BE are perpendicular. When triangle ABE is folded along AE, A and E do not move, and B corresponds to F, so AB corresponds to AF, BE corresponds to EF, and the right-angle relationship is preserved, so AF⊥EF. Also because F is on AC, AF and AC are collinear, therefore EF⊥AC. Folding preserves length, so AF=AB=x, EF=BE=1. The diagonal AC of the square forms a 45° angle with side BC. Since FC is on AC, EC is on BC, and EF⊥FC, triangle EFC is a right isosceles triangle, therefore FC=EF=1. Thus along diagonal AC there is AC=AF+FC=x+1. On the other hand, the side length of the square is x, so diagonal AC=x√2. Therefore x√2=x+1, obtaining x(√2-1)=1, so x=1/(√2-1)=1+√2. Therefore AB=1+√2.
